transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess I’ve been having some trouble with eating after work. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but after late shifts I’ll sometimes stop for takeout and get, like, two burgers, fries, a shake… and then I’ll still go home and pick at leftovers in the garage, almost like a second supper. I know that’s not great, so… I figured I should talk to someone.
Does this pattern of eating after work bother you or interfere with your daily life in any way?

I mean… I’m still getting to work fine, and I’m keeping up with church and all that, so it’s not like everything’s falling apart. But, yeah, I guess it does bother me some. At home I’ve been more… quiet, kind of withdrawn, because I’m using a lot of energy trying to cover where I stopped after work, or why I’m not hungry when dinner’s there. That part doesn’t feel great.
When you're eating like that after work, does it ever feel like you're not in control—like you can't stop eating even if you want to?

Yeah… I guess that’s probably the part I don’t like saying out loud. It’s not like I’m trying to be reckless, but once I start, it feels like some switch gets flipped. I’ll be telling myself, Roy, just shut the bag and go inside, you’ve had enough, and then my hands are still reaching for more anyway. If that makes sense.
Has this eating pattern affected your relationships, job performance, or caused you significant distress emotionally?

I wouldn’t say it’s hurt my job performance, exactly… I still show up and do what I’m supposed to do. But emotionally, yeah, it bothers me more than I probably let on.

Afterward I feel pretty ashamed, kind of disgusted with myself, honestly. I’ve always tried to be disciplined and dependable, you know, and this makes me feel like I’m sneaking around and letting myself down. I don’t like admitting that, but… that’s probably the truth.
After these episodes of eating that you’ve described, do you ever try to compensate for it—like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t made myself sick or anything like that, and I’m not taking stuff to undo it.

Sometimes I’ll tell myself I ought to “make up for it” somehow, but I don’t really go do some big workout or anything. Mostly I just feel bad about it and try to act normal, if that makes sense.
Can you tell me more about what it feels like when you start eating—does it happen quickly, like you suddenly find yourself eating a lot without really meaning to?

Yeah… it can be pretty quick, I guess. I don’t always go into it thinking, I’m going to eat a lot. It’s more like once I start, something kind of takes over.

I’ll be telling myself, Roy, shut the bag, go inside, that’s enough, and then… my hands are still reaching for more. I know that probably sounds strange, but that’s how it feels in the moment—like I mean to stop, but I’m not really stopping.
Do you usually eat these larger amounts of food when you’re alone, or in secret?

Yeah… more often than I’d like to admit, I guess.

I mean, I don’t usually do it right in front of my wife. I’ll act like I’m not all that hungry at dinner, like everything’s normal, and then later I might go out to the truck or wait until she’s busy with something. It’s embarrassing to say, but I don’t want her seeing how much I’m actually putting away.

I know that sounds kind of sneaky… I’m not proud of it.
When you're eating in these moments, does it feel like you're watching yourself do it but can't stop, like you're not really in control of your actions?

Yeah… I think that’s a fair way to put it. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I start, it’s like some switch flips.

I’ll be thinking, Roy, shut the bag, go back inside, that’s enough… and then I’m still reaching in for more anyway. It’s embarrassing, because I know what I should be doing, but in that moment I don’t really feel like I’m the one steering it, if that makes sense.
Can you describe what it's like just before you start eating in these moments—do you feel like you're making a choice, or does it feel more like something you can't control?

I guess… before it starts, I’d like to think I’m choosing it, you know? Like I’m just going to have a little bit and then stop.

But honestly, once I start, it doesn’t feel that simple. It’s like the switch is flipped, and even while I’m telling myself, Roy, shut the bag and go inside, my hands just keep reaching for more. I know that probably sounds like an excuse, and I don’t mean it that way… it just doesn’t feel like I’m fully in control right then.
Can you recall if, during these episodes, you feel like you’re not able to stop eating even if you want to, like you’re not in control once you start?

Yeah… yes, I think that’s exactly it.

I don’t like saying “out of control,” because that sounds pretty bad, but once I start, it feels like that switch gets flipped. I’ll be telling myself, Roy, shut the bag, go back inside, that’s enough… and then I’m still reaching for more anyway.

So, yeah… even when I want to stop, in that moment it doesn’t really feel like I can.
How often would you say you experience these episodes where you feel like you lose control while eating, even if just for a short time?

Um… I guess it’s not every day or anything. But for the past few months, there’s usually at least one night a week where it happens.

And if I’m being honest, some weeks it’s more like two or three nights… usually after a late shift or if it’s been a rough day on the line. I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you mean.
When these episodes happen, do they usually take place within a short time, like a couple of hours, or does the eating stretch out much longer?

It’s usually not all night or anything like that… more like it happens in one stretch, I guess.

Like after a late shift, I’ll stop for takeout thinking it’s just dinner, and then I’ll end up eating… more than I meant to. Two burgers, fries, a shake—then I get home and, sometimes, I’m still picking at leftovers out in the garage, like it’s another meal.

That’s embarrassing to say. But time-wise, yeah, it’s usually kind of all packed into that evening, not stretched out over the whole day.
Do these episodes cause you a lot of distress, even when they’re over, like guilt, shame, or feeling like you’ve failed yourself?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to make a huge thing out of it, but yes. Afterward I feel pretty ashamed.

It’s like… I’ve always thought of myself as a disciplined person, dependable, you know? I show up, I do what I’m supposed to do. And then when I do this, especially if I’m kind of hiding it or sneaking around with it, I feel… disgusted with myself, I guess.

Like I let myself down. I don’t know if that sounds too dramatic, but that’s how it feels afterward.
Can you describe exactly what it feels like in the moment when you feel like you can't stop eating, and whether it feels different from just choosing to eat more than you planned?

Yeah… it does feel different. I mean, I know there are times anybody eats more than they meant to, right? Like, that’s not what I’m trying to make sound worse than it is.

But in those moments, it’s more like… once I start, something flips. I’ll be thinking, Roy, just close the bag and go inside. You’ve had enough. And at the same time, my hand is already reaching back in for more.

So it’s not like I’m sitting there calmly deciding, “Sure, I’ll have another.” It feels more… automatic, I guess. Like I’m arguing with myself and still doing it anyway. Does that make sense?
Do you find yourself feeling very upset or distressed specifically about these episodes of eating, even when they’re over?

Yeah… I do. I don’t want to overstate it, but it does hit me pretty hard afterward.

I feel ashamed, mostly. Kind of disgusted with myself, if I’m being honest. I’ve always thought of myself as someone who’s disciplined, dependable… and then after one of those times, especially if I was sneaking around with it, it feels like I really let myself down.

I know that probably sounds harsh, but that’s where my head goes.
